_comment: Curated choices for CLOSED-CLASS words (demonstratives, interrogatives, pronouns). Frequency ranking is the wrong tool here: there are only a few dozen of these, they appear constantly, and the dictionary's glosses mislead. 'that' ranked 'tamto' first because it is glossed exactly 'that', while the general demonstrative 'tȯj' is glossed 'this, that' and so looked like a worse match - but tamto means 'that OVER THERE'. Each entry below is justified against a cited source rather than chosen by score.
_scope: Closed classes, plus open-class words only for a sense the parse itself shows (whenDependent, unlessHeadIs). The other senses of such a word stay with dictionary ranking - curating open-class words wholesale would never end.

words.why: the plain distal demonstrative; 'tamto' means 'that over there'
words.evidence: steenbergen-syntax: 'Kde otec kupil tu knigu?' = 'Where did father buy that book?'; 'Koja žena ljubi togo muža?' = 'Which woman loves that man?'

words.why: the proximal demonstrative (the dictionary's lemma is the etymological `tutȯj`; written `tutoj` here it never matched, and ranking chose instead)
words.evidence: steenbergen-syntax: 'Tutoj hlěb jest nedragy.' = 'This bread is inexpensive.'

words.why: used in the grammar's own interrogative examples; 'ktory' is also correct and is ranked type 1, so this is a preference rather than a correction
words.evidence: steenbergen-syntax: 'Koju knigu kupil otec?'; 'Koja žena ljubi togo muža?'

words.why: 'too' modifying a verb or a clause means 'also'. Ranking took `zamnogo` ('too' as in 'too much', the Dutch 'te, te veel'), so 'I want to be a good artist, too' ended in 'zamnogo'; modifying an adjective ('too big') it is still that degree word
words.evidence: dictionary: takože adv. type 1 'also, too, as well'; zamnogo adv. 'too' (nl 'te, te veel'). Tatoeba 13522870 / 13525294: 'I want to be a good artist, too.' -> 'Ja tož hoču byti dobra artistka.'

words.why: the plain demonstrative. `tamtȯj` ('that over there', type 3) won on the exact gloss 'тот', where tȯj is glossed 'этот, тот'
words.evidence: steenbergen-pronouns: 'The primary demonstrative pronoun is toj “this, that”, and it should be used whenever there is no need to distinguish explicitly between this one over here and that one over there.' The English 'that' is curated the same way

words.why: the first half of the reciprocal 'друг друга/другу/...' (PronType=Rcp): the formula is 'jedin drugogo', with drugy in the case the second half carries. The dictionary glosses only the genitive 'друг друга', so 'друг другу' became 'prijatelj prijatelju'
words.evidence: steenbergen-pronouns: 'you can add the formula jedin drugogo: „Oni bijut se jedin drugogo”'; his Tower of Babel: 'I oni govorili jedin k drugomu', 'da by oni ne razuměli se jedin drugogo'

words.why: the second half of the reciprocal, in its own case: 'другу' -> 'drugomu'
words.evidence: steenbergen-pronouns: 'jedin drugogo'; his Tower of Babel: 'jedin k drugomu'

words.why: the neuter of 'тот', which the parser lemmatises separately ('от того, что задумали' -> lemma 'то'); the same plain demonstrative
words.evidence: steenbergen-pronouns: 'The primary demonstrative pronoun is toj “this, that”'

words.why: the universal 'all'. `cěly` is 'whole, entire' and won on the gloss 'весь', which the dictionary lists for both
words.evidence: steenbergen-pronouns: 'ves (f. vsa, n. vse “whole, entire; all”)', nominative plural masculine animate 'vsi'; van Steenbergen's UDHR Article 1: 'Vsi ljudi rodęt sę svobodni'

words.why: the possessive 'his/its', not an oblique form of the personal pronoun. It declines, so it can agree with the noun it modifies
words.evidence: steenbergen-pronouns: 'Pjotr dal Ivanu jegovu knigu' = 'Pjotr gave Ivan his [= Ivan's] book'. Ranking gave `nju` ('her', accusative) because the dictionary glosses oblique forms as entries of their own

words.why: the possessive 'her/hers'; the declinable form, so it agrees with its noun
words.evidence: steenbergen-pronouns: the possessives are listed as jegov / jejin / jihny beside the indeclinable jego / jej / jih

words.why: the possessive 'their'; the declinable form, so it agrees with its noun
words.evidence: steenbergen-pronouns: the possessives are listed as jegov / jejin / jihny beside the indeclinable jego / jej / jih

words.why: the negative existential, glossed 'there is/are no'. The interjection `ne` ('no') is far more frequent and was winning, giving the verbless 'U mene ne brata'
words.evidence: the dictionary glosses `nema` and `nemaje` exactly 'there is/are no, there is/are not'; `ne` is glossed 'no' as an intj. and 'not' as an adv.

words.why: the interrogative 'which' in a question. `ktory` is also pron.int. and wins on frequency, but the pronouns page reserves it for RELATIVE clauses - and the English side already produces `koj` here, so this aligns the two source languages
words.evidence: steenbergen-syntax: 'Koju knigu kupil otec?' = 'Which book has father bought?'; 'Koja žena ljubi togo muža?' = 'Which woman loves that man?'. steenbergen-pronouns: 'The relative pronoun that is used most frequently is ktory'

words.why: under negation English 'a single' is a positive-polarity indefinite; Interslavic negates it, so 'not ... a single book' is 'ne ... nijednu knigu'. Dictionary ranking chose `jednokratny` ('one-time') because 'single' is its first gloss
words.evidence: steenbergen-syntax: 'Unlike in English, all negatable words are being negated in Interslavic, for example: - Ja uze nikogda ne budu citati nijednu knigu! „I am never going to read a single book anymore!”'

words.why: the dictionary pairs this as the multiword `uz ne` glossed 'not anymore'; the `ne` half is the clause negation the negation pass already emits, so only `uze` is this word's own contribution. Left untranslated it printed the English 'anymore' in Interslavic output
words.evidence: steenbergen-syntax: 'Unlike in English, all negatable words are being negated in Interslavic, for example: - Ja uze nikogda ne budu citati nijednu knigu! „I am never going to read a single book anymore!”'

words.why: a floor counted by a numeral is a storey of a building. The dictionary glosses `etaž` only as 'storey', so 'floor' always reached `podloga` (the surface walked on), which stays the choice when nothing counts it
words.evidence: steenbergen-numerals: 'Dom s tri etažami „A house with three floors”'

words.why: a party one comes to or is at is an event, `zabava`. `partija` is the political party; both are glossed bare 'party' and are type 1, so no dictionary column separates them, and frequency chose `partija`
words.evidence: steenbergen-syntax: 'Nikto ne prijehal na zabavu. „Nobody came to the party.”'; steenbergen-numerals: 'zabava v troje „a party for three”'; the political sense on steenbergen-orthography: 'Komunistična partija Sovětskogo Sojuza'

words.why: work one goes to, is at or comes from is the job, `råbota` ('job, work, employment'). `dělo` is glossed bare 'work' and so outranks it on gloss position, but its sense is the work produced - its other rows are 'act, deed' and 'affair'
words.evidence: steenbergen-verbs: 'Iduči do raboty, ona vsegda dymi cigaretoju „While going to her work, she always smokes a cigarette”'; the dictionary's own usage example for råbota: 'Iz pričiny intensivnosti raboty'

words.why: as for English "work": the work one goes to, is at or comes from (на/в/с/из/до работе/работу/работы) is the job, `råbota`. The dictionary lists `dělo` first for "работа", but its sense is the work produced
words.evidence: steenbergen-verbs: 'Iduči do raboty, ona vsegda dymi cigaretoju „While going to her work, she always smokes a cigarette”'; the dictionary's own usage example for råbota: 'Iz pričiny intensivnosti raboty'

words.why: an indefinite cardinal number, which puts its noun in the genitive (numeral.government.indefinite). English tags 'many' as an adjective, so ranking by part of speech chose the adjective `mnogy`, giving 'mnoge knigy'
words.evidence: steenbergen-numerals: 'so-called indefinite cardinal numbers, consisting of words like mnogo „much, many”, malo „little, few”'

words.why: an indefinite cardinal number, which puts its noun in the genitive (numeral.government.indefinite). English tags 'much' as an adjective, so ranking by part of speech chose the adjective `mnogy`, giving 'mnoge knigy'
words.evidence: steenbergen-numerals: 'so-called indefinite cardinal numbers, consisting of words like mnogo „much, many”, malo „little, few”'

words.why: an indefinite cardinal number, which puts its noun in the genitive (numeral.government.indefinite). English tags 'few' as an adjective, so ranking by part of speech chose `maly` 'small, little', which would say 'small people'
words.evidence: steenbergen-numerals: 'so-called indefinite cardinal numbers, consisting of words like mnogo „much, many”, malo „little, few”'

words.why: driving around is going by transport with no single direction, which the verbs page gives as the non-directional `jezditi` (directional `jehati`, perfective `pojehati`). `voziti sę` is glossed 'drive (e.g. by car)' and is chosen otherwise; the page lists `voziti` as 'to transport'
words.evidence: steenbergen-verbs, the table of motion verbs (non-directional, directional, perfective): 'jezditi jehati pojehati'; 'Igor jezdil po Moskvě „Igor was driving around in Moscow”'

words.why: the dictionary glosses `izvini, izvinite` and `pomiluj` identically ("sorry, excuse me") and states no preference; ranking by intelligibility marks chose `pomiluj`. Where the dictionary is neutral, usage decides, and usage has izvini/izvinite 6 times and pomiluj never. The vy form, as the translator addresses the reader
words.evidence: Wp/isv phrase table "Извините! - Izvinite!" and "Nu izvini" (talk page); Tatoeba (isv) "Govori \"izvini\"!", "Govorite \"izvinite\"!"; pomiluj: 0 in both
